C-MANAGED-SKILLS-CANONICAL-GRAMMAR.Summary: Replace the ad-hoc per-skill XML envelope in all eleven managed skills with one canonical six-block grammar: frontmatter then scope, workflow, rules, optional artifact, optional refs, and done. Remove the universal skill root, identity, and task blocks; keep rule and step elements only where they are addressed or referenced; fold unique identity content into scope and the completion half of task into done; unify the execution-mode vocabulary between vv-plan and vv-execute; repair reference drift; and gate the grammar with deterministic tests.
C-MANAGED-SKILLS-CANONICAL-GRAMMAR.Problem: The eleven SKILL.md templates were copied from a single 2026-05 envelope and drifted independently. All eleven carry an identity block and ten carry a task block; combined they occupy 7-13 percent of each body and restate the same normative rule two to four times (for example, vv-reflect states one approval rule in identity, approval, and write_rules). The block vocabulary is ad hoc: about thirty names, two naming conventions (snake_case and kebab-case), attributes used as labels, rule meaning both a constraint and a procedure step, scope carrying five unrelated meanings, and completion carrying both archival sequencing and stop/blocked reporting. None of the tags is parsed by the runtime, so no test detects drift. Cross-skill behavior has already diverged: vv-plan offers workflow tracked loop, delegated, and manual execution options while vv-execute and the plan linter accept only inline, classic, and delegated. Six hand-authored markdown references exceed one hundred lines without a table of contents. vvoc-usage-analytics pins its database notes to OpenCode 1.18.x while the package supports 2.0.18 and newer. The result is a collection that reads as XML-shaped prose: the markup separates blocks visually but does not give the model a small, stable vocabulary it can rely on in long sessions.

Goals.Goal: Define one canonical skill grammar: YAML frontmatter, then scope, workflow, rules, optional artifact, optional refs, and done in that fixed order; snake_case element names; no skill root; no identity or task blocks; markdown prose, lists, and tables inside the blocks; XML reserved for addressable structure and literal artifact templates.

Keep rule as the normative unit inside rules, and use step only when a workflow step is addressed by name or referenced elsewhere. Permit exactly one attribute per addressable element: name on step and id on rule. No other attributes.

Preserve every normative obligation while deleting restatements. Unique identity content moves into scope: the three execution modes and their ownership boundary, the plan-is-contracts-not-implementations rule, the no-delegation rule in vv-spec, the guidance-not-a-linter stance, and the routing and read-only boundaries of review, reflect, handoff, analytics, and UI work. The completion condition and evidence from task move into done.
Unify execution vocabulary to inline, classic, and delegated across vv-plan and vv-execute so the plan handoff cannot offer a mode that the executor and the plan linter reject.
Give vv-execute one authoritative mode and ownership table, one authoritative commit discipline shared by all three workflows, and a refs entry for the generated tool-contracts reference.

Repair reference drift: add a table of contents to the six references longer than one hundred lines while preserving their existing headings; state the vvoc-usage-analytics database validation provenance together with the supported OpenCode window instead of implying the validated version is current.

Add a deterministic grammar gate that scans every managed template and reference for the allowed block set and order, banned blocks, attribute policy, frontmatter and directory agreement, reference existence, one-level references, and table-of-contents coverage, with synthetic negative fixtures proving the gate rejects violations.

Keep skill names, frontmatter descriptions, trigger conditions, install and sync semantics, file counts, and the vv-write-for-agents volume budget unchanged so routing and the packaged surface do not move.

Record the current skill-authoring criteria the change satisfies structurally — name and description limits, bodies under five hundred lines, one-level references, contents sections for long references, no stale time-sensitive claims, and consistent terminology — and state explicitly that behavioral evaluation is out of scope.

Constraints.Constraint: Behavior preservation is normative: every current obligation, hard stop, approval gate, evidence requirement, tool contract, and output format remains in force after the rewrite. The change is a re-serialization and de-duplication, not a policy change.

Frontmatter descriptions stay byte-identical. Skill names, the MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES registry, install and sync behavior, the 33-file and 31-file installed surface counts, and README skill rows do not change.
Do not add reference files or runtime modules. The grammar gate lives in a colocated test file and uses no production parser.
The vv-write-for-agents budget remains: SKILL.md at most 80 lines, total shipped text at most 420 lines, no .grace or M-/V-/GD- anchors in its shipped files.

Hand-authored references remain markdown documents loaded one level deep from SKILL.md. Spec, plan, and handoff artifact templates remain XML because those artifacts are XML. The generated tool-contracts reference, the XML plan and spec templates, the Python session-graph extractor, and any other non-markdown reference are exempt from markdown rewriting and from the contents-section rule.
Markdown headings are permitted inside workflow and artifact to separate named sub-procedures; they do not create new top-level blocks and are not part of the grammar allowlist.

The only permitted attributes are name on step and id on rule, and only when another block references that step or rule. Attributes used as decorative labels are removed in favor of element names, tables, or list items.
Tests assert instruction delivery and structure, not model effectiveness. No artifact may claim that XML improves adherence or that the gate proves model behavior.

Graph and verification projections are reconciled inside this approved change lifecycle. Archived C-* bundles, generated dist output, user-owned config, plugins, agents, the workflow engine, the config schema, and release automation stay untouched.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No behavioral evaluation of XML versus markdown, no A/B prompt study, and no claim of measured adherence improvement.
No new skill, no skill rename, no description or trigger rewrite, and no change to managed-agent prompts.
No rewrite of reference bodies beyond the table of contents and the vvoc-usage-analytics version-provenance sentence.
No new runtime parser, CLI command, lint command, plugin behavior, or config key for skill grammar.
No README change unless a description or user-facing behavior actually changes, which this change does not intend.
No changes to the workflow engine, plugins, native config, model roles, presets, release automation, or archived history.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: All eleven templates begin with YAML frontmatter followed directly by scope; none contains a skill root, identity, task, principle, language, or completion block; every top-level block is one of scope, workflow, rules, artifact, refs, done, in that order, with scope, workflow, rules, and done present.

AC-02: Element names use snake_case only. No attributes appear except name on step and id on rule, and each such attribute is referenced by another block or is necessary to identify the step being discussed; decorative attributes such as mode name, option name, source precedence, and step labels without references are gone.

AC-03: Unique identity content survives in scope: vv-execute retains the three modes and the controller-versus-worker ownership boundary; vv-plan retains the contract-level-not-implementation rule; vv-spec retains no-subagent-delegation and the interview responsibility; vv-write-for-agents retains guidance-not-a-linter and the whole-effective-input framing; vv-verification retains evidence-not-test-count; vv-review, vv-reflect, vv-handoff, vvoc-usage-analytics, and vv-ui-design-principles retain their routing, read-only, and authority boundaries.

AC-04: Every skill ends with a done block that states the completion condition, the required evidence, and the stop or blocked behavior. vvoc-usage-analytics, which previously had no task block, gains one. No done block merely restates the workflow.

AC-05: vv-plan offers exactly inline, classic, and delegated execution intent and offers exactly those three options at handoff; the strings workflow tracked loop and manual execution are absent; the vocabulary matches vv-execute and the plan linter vocabulary inline, classic, delegated.

AC-06: vv-execute defines each mode and its ownership boundary once in an artifact table, resolves mode selection once in rules, and reuses those definitions in the three workflows; commit discipline is stated once, preserves the classic derivation order and its omit-if-unavailable fallback, applies the same discipline to inline commits, and excludes internal T-NNN identifiers; refs lists the generated tool-contracts reference with its load condition.

AC-07: The six hand-authored markdown references longer than one hundred lines — vv-verification/evidence.md, oracles.md, strategy.md, create-your-verification-stack.md, vv-ui-design-principles/slop-tells.md, and vvoc-usage-analytics/opencode-db-queries.md — carry a contents section at the top and keep their existing headings. The generated tool-contracts reference, plan-template.xml, design-context-template.xml, spec-template.xml, and session-graph.py are outside this rule.

AC-08: vvoc-usage-analytics states that the database snippets were validated against OpenCode 1.18.x and that the supported window is 2.0.18 and newer, and instructs the agent to report a schema mismatch instead of improvising when a column fails.

AC-09: A colocated grammar test scans all eleven template bodies after removing YAML frontmatter, CDATA sections, fenced code blocks, and inline code, and fails on a banned block, an out-of-order block, an unapproved attribute, a kebab-case element, a missing required block, a frontmatter name that disagrees with its directory, a referenced file that does not exist, a reference file not listed in refs, a nested reference directory, or a hand-authored markdown reference over one hundred lines without a contents section. Generated tool-contracts.md, XML templates, and the Python extractor are explicitly exempt from the contents rule. Synthetic negative fixtures prove each rejection path independently of the shipped templates.

AC-10: Existing content-marker tests in src/lib/managed-skills.test.ts are updated to the new serialization while preserving the obligations they pin, including review-only routing, the VVOC_WORK_ITEM_ID launch contract, execution acceptance and recovery, execution intent and checkpoints, verification anchors, bilingual patterns, and the vv-write-for-agents volume and banned-token budget. The tests pass with fresh output.

AC-11: The M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS graph purpose and the V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS verification scenario describe the canonical grammar and its gate; the new grammar test file is listed among the verification test files and its command among the checks; grace lint and grace status report no new errors or warnings.

AC-12: The full repository gate passes with fresh output: bun run check, bun run build, bun run pack:check, grace lint, grace status, and git diff --check. The diff contains only the approved template, reference, test, and GRACE lifecycle files.

AC-13: The plan records the skill-authoring best-practice checklist the change satisfies structurally — the name and description limits, bodies under five hundred lines, one-level references, contents sections for long references, no stale time-sensitive claims, and consistent terminology — and explicitly marks behavioral evaluation of XML versus markdown as out of scope.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The grammar test demonstrates that every shipped template conforms and that each forbidden shape is rejected by a synthetic fixture. The content-marker tests demonstrate that the obligations survived the reserialization. Pack and build demonstrate that the templates are still shipped. GRACE lint and status demonstrate that the graph and verification projections remain truthful. These checks prove delivery and structure, not model behavior; no adherence claim is made.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user selected the XML-like format on 2026-11-24 and explicitly chose to remove the skill root and to keep rule and step elements where addressability is needed. This specification implements that decision rather than the earlier markdown-native recommendation.
Frontmatter descriptions remain unchanged, so OpenCode routing and the README managed-skill rows stay accurate without edits.
The vvoc-usage-analytics version fix preserves 1.18.x as validation provenance and adds the supported window; it does not claim the snippets were revalidated against 2.x.

The scope and workflow blocks are required in every skill so the model can always find boundaries, ordered behavior, and a completion condition. Artifact and refs stay optional because not every skill emits a structured artifact or loads a reference.

The user explicitly instructed creation of the spec and plan bundle on 2026-11-24, which is recorded as approval of this normative spec. The plan remains draft until the requested reviewers report and the user approves execution; implementation, commit, and installation follow only after that approval.
